n62539108d7b.s: Monsoon failure driving rural workers towards cities is an example of:
n62539108d7b.x: Monsoon failure is a rural disadvantage that pushes people out of villages, so it is a push factor.

n0a5077cd01c.s: Under the 16th Finance Commission, the share of urban local bodies in local body grants is raised to:
n0a5077cd01c.x: The 16th FC raises the ULB share to 45%, up from 36% under the 15th FC.

n6169d13d402.s: Which of the following phases of urbanisation in India is NOT correctly matched with its period?
n6169d13d402.x: The medium phase was 1931-1961; the period from 1961 onwards is the rapid phase.

nceca033e486.s: How many functions does the Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution assign to municipalities?
nceca033e486.x: The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 functions relating to urban local governance.

ne1211c75fc2.s: Which of the following urban schemes was launched first?
ne1211c75fc2.x: JNNURM came in December 2005, well before SBM-Urban (2 October 2014) and AMRUT (June 2015).

n4855526fede.s: Which PMAY-U vertical is NOT part of PMAY-U 2.0?
n4855526fede.x: PMAY-U 2.0 has BLC, AHP, Affordable Rental Housing and the Interest Subsidy Scheme; ISSR belonged only to the earlier PMAY-U.

n2437322a03d.s: Basic Services to the Urban Poor (BSUP) was a component of which mission?
n2437322a03d.x: BSUP and IHSDP were the two components of JNNURM; CLSS and ISSR belong to PMAY-U.

nb8309434193.s: Andhra Pradesh signed its MoU on urban affairs with:
nb8309434193.x: AP's urban-affairs MoU was signed with UN-Habitat, not UNESCO.

n7c1c868b9b0.s: Ajmer qualified as an AMRUT mission city of Rajasthan because it is a:
o: City on the stem of a main river
n7c1c868b9b0.x: Ajmer qualified as a HRIDAY city; Jaipur qualified as the State capital and Jodhpur by its 1 lakh+ population.

na3d5ed27f87.s: Household out-of-pocket expenditure in 2022-23 was what share of total health expenditure?
na3d5ed27f87.x: OOPE was 43.4% of total health expenditure in 2022-23 (176th Report of the Standing Committee on Health).

n9c4731e229c.s: AB-PMJAY was launched on 23 September 2018 at:
n9c4731e229c.x: AB-PMJAY was launched at Ranchi (Jharkhand) on 23 September 2018.

new.s: Which State has the largest number of statutory towns as per Census 2011?
new.x: Uttar Pradesh has the most statutory towns (648); Tamil Nadu has the most towns overall (statutory + census).

new.s: Which State has the largest total number of towns (statutory plus census) as per Census 2011?
new.x: Tamil Nadu has the most towns when statutory and census towns are counted together.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about towns in Census 2011:
1. There were about 4,041 statutory towns.
2. There were 3,892 census towns.
3. Census towns numbered 1,362 in 2011.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: 2011 had about 4,041 statutory and 3,892 census towns; 1,362 was the census-town count of 2001.

new.s: Under Census classification, towns of Class IV, V and VI are together called:
new.x: Class IV, V and VI towns (under 20,000 population) are the small towns.

new.s: Indian cities occupy about 3% of land but generate roughly what share of GDP?
new.x: Cities cover about 3% of India's land and produce about 60% of its GDP.

new.s: The share of India's urban population rose from about 11% in 1901 to about ____ in 2011.
new.x: India's urban share rose from 11% in 1901 to 31.1% in 2011.

new.s: As per Census 2011, which State had the largest urban population in absolute numbers?
new.x: Maharashtra had the largest urban population (5.08 crore), followed by Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

new.s: As per Census 2011, which State had the smallest urban population in absolute numbers?
new.x: Sikkim had the smallest urban population (1,53,578), below Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland and Mizoram.

new.s: Which State had no million-plus city as per Census 2011?
new.x: Odisha had no million-plus city; Haryana had Faridabad, J&K Srinagar and Jharkhand Jamshedpur, Dhanbad and Ranchi.

new.s: Million-plus cities held what share of India's urban population in 2011?
new.x: Million-plus cities held 42.6% of the urban population in 2011, up from 37.8% in 2001.

new.s: Which region was the most urbanised in 2020 as per World Cities Report 2024?
new.x: Australia/New Zealand was most urbanised at 86.3%, ahead of North America at 82.6%.

new.s: India's urban population is projected to reach about how much by 2031?
new.x: India is projected to have about 60 crore urban people by 2031.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about causes of urbanisation:
1. Monsoon failure is a push factor.
2. Magnetic features of cities are a pull factor.
3. Rural-urban imbalance is a push factor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Monsoon failure and rural-urban imbalance push people out of villages; jobs and amenities of cities pull them in.

new.s: Philip M. Hauser used the term 'Population Implosion' to describe:
new.x: Hauser called the rural-urban concentration of people 'Population Implosion'; the 'New Population Bomb' is the fast-growing Third World urban population.

new.s: The urban housing shortage estimated by the 2012 Technical Group is about:
new.x: The 2012 Technical Group put the urban housing shortage at about 18.78 million units.

new.s: The urban heat island effect raises city temperatures by about:
new.x: The urban heat island effect makes cities about 3-5°C warmer.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 16th Finance Commission (2026-31):
1. Urban local bodies get 45% of local body grants.
2. Grants are split 80% basic and 20% performance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The 16th FC gives ULBs 45% (Rs 3.6 lakh crore) and splits grants 80% basic and 20% performance.

new.s: The Local Finance Enquiry Committee of 1963 was headed by K. Santhanam; A.D. Gorwala (1951) examined:
new.x: A.D. Gorwala's 1951 committee dealt with rural credit; K. Santhanam's 1963 committee dealt with local finance.

new.s: APMCHUD, the Asia-Pacific Ministerial Conference on Housing and Urban Development, first met at:
new.x: The first APMCHUD meeting was held in New Delhi in 2006.

new.s: Where is the headquarters of UN-Habitat?
new.x: UN-Habitat, set up in 1978, has its headquarters in Nairobi.

new.s: Habitat I, after which UN-Habitat was set up, was held at:
new.x: Habitat I was held at Vancouver in 1976; UN-Habitat followed in 1978.

new.s: How many municipal corporations does Andhra Pradesh have?
new.x: Andhra Pradesh has 17 municipal corporations among its 123 ULBs.

new.s: On the 2011 Census base, the urban share of residuary Andhra Pradesh is about:
new.x: Residuary AP was 29.6% urban; 33.4% was the figure for undivided AP.

new.s: Which of the following were launched on the same day, 25 June 2015?
o: AMRUT, Smart Cities Mission and PMAY-U
JNNURM, AMRUT and Smart Cities Mission
new.x: AMRUT, the Smart Cities Mission and PMAY-U were all launched on 25 June 2015; SBM-Urban came earlier on 2 October 2014.

new.s: Which of the following missions has a rural rather than urban focus?
new.x: The Rurban Mission (SPMRM, 2016) develops rural-urban clusters and has a rural focus; the rest are urban.

new.s: HRIDAY was launched on:
new.x: HRIDAY was launched on 21 January 2015 by MoHUA.

new.s: JNNURM was a programme of how many years?
new.x: JNNURM, launched on 3 December 2005, was a 7-year programme.

new.s: Under JNNURM reforms, what share of developed land was to be reserved for EWS/LIG?
new.x: JNNURM reforms reserved 25% of developed land for EWS/LIG.

new.s: Under the Garbage Free City star rating, which certification is the prerequisite for a 5-Star rating?
new.x: 5-Star needs ODF++; 1-Star needs ODF, 3-Star ODF+ and 7-Star Water+.

new.s: Which Andhra Pradesh city is in the Super Swachh League (10 lakh+ group) of Swachh Survekshan 2024-25?
new.x: Vijayawada is in the Super Swachh League with Indore, Surat and Navi Mumbai.

new.s: Which city was ranked the 'cleanest big city' (10 lakh+) in Swachh Survekshan 2024-25?
new.x: Ahmedabad was ranked cleanest big city, followed by Bhopal and Lucknow; Indore was placed in the Super Swachh League.

new.s: SBM-Urban 2.0, aimed at garbage-free cities, was launched on:
new.x: SBM-U 2.0 was launched on 1 October 2021.

new.s: AMRUT covers about what share of India's urban population?
new.x: AMRUT covers about 60% of the urban population through its 485 cities.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an AMRUT thrust area?
new.x: Crop procurement is not an AMRUT thrust area; drains, parks and capacity building are.

new.s: How many cities were selected under the Smart Cities Mission?
new.x: The Smart Cities Mission selected 100 cities through a competitive challenge; AMRUT has 500 (now 485).

new.s: Under the Smart Cities Mission, a city's SPV is a company incorporated under:
new.x: Each Smart City SPV is a company under the Companies Act, 2013.

new.s: Smart Cities were selected in how many rounds starting January 2016?
new.x: Selection was through four rounds from January 2016; the last city came in June 2018.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT among the 12 HRIDAY cities?
new.x: Agra is not a HRIDAY city; Warangal, Amaravati and Puri are.

new.s: Which PMAY-U vertical is a Central Sector scheme?
new.x: CLSS is the only Central Sector vertical; ISSR, AHP and BLC are Centrally Sponsored.

new.s: Light House Projects under GHTC-India had their foundation laid in January 2021 in cities including:
new.x: Light House Project cities are Indore, Rajkot, Chennai, Ranchi, Agartala and Lucknow.

new.s: PMAY-U 2.0 (2024) aims to provide how many more urban houses?
new.x: PMAY-U 2.0 targets 1 crore more urban houses; 1.25 crore+ is the sanctions figure under both phases.

new.s: The Urban Infrastructure Development Fund was announced in:
new.x: UIDF was announced in the Union Budget 2023-24.

new.s: The Urban Infrastructure Development Fund has a size of about:
new.x: UIDF is about Rs 10,000 crore a year.

new.s: Under Swachh Andhra (2024-25), waste segregation in Andhra Pradesh reached about:
new.x: Waste segregation under Swachh Andhra was 96.07% in 2024-25.

new.s: Anna Canteens in Andhra Pradesh were reopened in:
new.x: Anna Canteens, serving meals at Rs 5, reopened in August 2024.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT among Andhra Pradesh's four Smart Cities?
new.x: AP's four Smart Cities are Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Tirupati and Amaravati; Vijayawada is not one.

new.s: Which of the following does NOT have a direct impact on human capital formation?
new.x: Irrigation does not directly form human capital; skills, health and migration do.

new.s: India's stunting rate, cited among human capital indicators, is about:
new.x: Stunting is 29.3% and wasting 19%.

new.s: National Health Policy 2017 targets public health spending of what share of GDP by 2025?
new.x: NHP 2017 targets 2.5% of GDP by 2025; 6% is the NEP 2020 education target.

new.s: Government health expenditure in India, per the 176th Report of the Standing Committee on Health, is about:
new.x: Government health spending is 1.43% of GDP against the 2.5% target; 4.89% is the health share of government spending.

new.s: The 'missing middle' in Indian health financing covers about how many people?
new.x: The missing middle is 40 crore+ Indians outside full subsidy cover who cannot afford private care.

new.s: The Ayushman Vay Vandana card under PM-JAY covers:
o: All persons aged 60+ below the poverty line
All persons aged 70+ regardless of income
new.x: Announced on 29 October 2024, it gives Rs 5 lakh cover to everyone aged 70+, with no income test.

new.s: Which States were the latest to join PM-JAY in April 2025?
new.x: Odisha and Delhi were the latest to join PM-JAY, in April 2025.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT among the four registries of ABDM?
new.x: ABDM's four registries are ABHA, HPR, HFR and the Drug Registry; Integrated Public Health Labs are part of PM-ABHIM.

new.s: Creating an ABHA health ID under ABDM is:
new.x: ABHA is voluntary and consent-based, not mandatory.

new.s: ABDM was first announced as the National Digital Health Mission on:
new.x: NDHM was announced on 15 August 2020; ABDM was launched in September 2021.

new.s: Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK), launched in 2014, targets:
new.x: RKSK targets adolescents aged 10-19.

new.s: Janani Suraksha Yojana (2005) gives cash assistance to pregnant women for:
o: Antenatal check-ups on the 9th of each month
new.x: JSY gives cash for institutional delivery; free antenatal care on the 9th is PMSMA.

new.s: In which year did NRHM become a sub-mission of the National Health Mission?
new.x: NRHM, launched in 2005, became a sub-mission of NHM in 2013 along with NUHM.

new.s: The Education Commission of 1964 was chaired by:
new.x: D.S. Kothari chaired the 1964 Education Commission.

new.s: The University Education Commission of 1948 was chaired by:
new.x: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan chaired the 1948 commission; Dr K. Radhakrishnan headed the 2024 NTA committee.

new.s: The school structure under NEP 2020 is:
new.x: NEP 2020 replaces 10+2 with a 5+3+3+4 structure.

new.s: Which of the following schemes linked to NEP 2020 is NOT correctly matched?
o: NIPUN Bharat – foundational literacy and numeracy
new.x: PARAKH deals with assessment; school meals are under PM POSHAN.

new.s: NEP 2020 targets public education spending of:
new.x: NEP 2020 targets public spending on education of 6% of GDP.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's Family Physician programme was launched on:
new.x: The Family Doctor programme was launched on 6 April 2023.

new.s: The Aarogyasri health scheme of Andhra Pradesh is now called:
new.x: Aarogyasri is now named Dr NTR Vaidya Seva.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's Sanjeevani programme (from August 2026) is a:
new.x: Sanjeevani is a digital health programme with health profile, ABHA and telemedicine for every citizen.

new.s: Thalliki Vandanam in Andhra Pradesh provides how much per school child per year?
new.x: Thalliki Vandanam gives Rs 15,000 per child a year (Rs 13,000 DBT plus Rs 2,000 for school upkeep).

new.s: Jagananna Gorumudda in Andhra Pradesh enriches the mid-day meal under:
new.x: Jagananna Gorumudda (2020) is an enriched mid-day meal under PM POSHAN.
